commitResults.messageBody:
Task state and storage names are unclear, and Task fields expose mutable implementation details.

Rename Athena's task storage fields for clarity and make Task fields private,
keeping the description immutable while preserving task status behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mandate project coding and Git standards
commitResults.messageBody:
Project guidance needs to enforce the SE-EDU coding and Git conventions for future work.

Require agents to follow the project-specific Java and Git standards while
preserving the starter template's default-package layout.

Java contributions need a reusable project-specific reference for the SE-EDU coding conventions.

Add the skill and its interface metadata so future Java work applies the
required naming, layout, encapsulation, and documentation rules.

Commit and branch conventions need a reusable project-specific reference.

Add the skill and interface metadata so future commits use clear imperative
subjects, useful bodies, and meaningful branch names.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add Deadline, Event and Todo classes

commitResults.messageBody: Store only the Todo description instead of the full command line, and require an exact Todo command prefix so unrelated inputs are not classified as Todos.
Parse only valid Deadline commands, remove debug output, and report malformed input without corrupting the task count.
Keep each Event's times independently, validate the required /from and /to syntax, and reject malformed commands without corrupting the task list.

The task list size was encoded as an unexplained literal in the array declaration. Replace it with MAX_TASKS so the capacity is self-documenting and can be changed from one clearly named definition without altering runtime behavior.

Athena kept its task array and task count in static mutable fields, coupling all execution to one global session and making the application harder to test or reuse. Store session data in an Athena instance and make output operations instance-based so each session owns its state without changing the command-line behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Separate command dispatch from input parsing
commitResults.messageBody: The input parser handled reading input, recognizing commands, checking capacity, and mutating tasks in one method. Extract command dispatch into handleCommand so each method has one clear responsibility while preserving the existing command-line behavior.

Todo is a public task type whose purpose and construction were not documented. Add concise Javadocs so readers can understand that it represents tasks without an associated date or time without inspecting the implementation.

The main loop called nextLine without checking whether another input line existed, so a redirected or closed input stream could terminate Athena with an exception. Check hasNextLine before parsing each command so the program exits cleanly at end of input while retaining the existing farewell behavior.

The task-addition branch relied on an unbraced if statement even though its body spans multiple lines. Add braces to make the control flow explicit and prevent future edits from accidentally changing which statements are conditional.

commitResults.messageTitle: Normalize commands with a fixed locale
commitResults.messageBody: Command dispatch converted the same input line to lowercase separately for each branch, using the default locale. Normalize once with Locale.ROOT so command recognition is consistent across environments and avoids repeated work.

Several comments claimed that input was echoed or repeated the operation performed by the next statement. Remove these inaccurate and redundant comments so the source communicates intent through behavior and retains only documentation that adds context.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add delete method and refactor task-managing methods into TaskManager

commitResults.messageBody:
Athena currently recognizes commands and dispatches task operations itself, which gives the application entry point more than one responsibility.

Move that behavior into a dedicated Parser and let Athena delegate each input line to it. This establishes the parsing boundary required for the OOP refactor while preserving the existing command flow and user-visible behavior.

TaskManager currently stores tasks in its own array and updates the
count during command handling. This mixes collection mechanics with
persistence and user feedback.

Introduce TaskList to own capacity, ordering, indexed access,
insertion, and removal. TaskManager can now coordinate changes and
rollback through that API, while Output and Storage read the list
without accessing its backing array.

Parser currently dispatches every recognized command directly, so there
is no common abstraction for command execution or application exit.

Add an abstract Command contract with execute and isExit behavior, then
move the valid list operation into ListCommand. Starting with this
read-only command establishes the extension point without combining it
with riskier mutation or loop-control changes.

The todo, deadline, and event parser branches still dispatch directly
to TaskManager even though they share one task-creation workflow.

Represent that workflow with AddCommand and retain the complete command
text for execution. TaskManager continues to validate, save, and roll back
changes, preserving its existing transactional behavior while expanding
the command hierarchy in a focused step.

Parser still dispatches delete requests directly, leaving one more
state-changing operation outside the command hierarchy.

Represent deletion with DeleteCommand and retain the complete command
text for execution. TaskManager continues to validate the index, persist
the removal, and restore the task on failure, so this step changes the
dispatch boundary without changing transaction semantics.

Parser still chooses the desired completion state with a boolean while
dispatching mark and unmark directly to TaskManager.

Introduce separate MarkCommand and UnmarkCommand types so each user
intent carries its own execution behavior. TaskManager retains shared
validation, persistence, and rollback, avoiding duplication of the
transaction while removing the status decision from Parser.

Parser previously created and executed commands itself. This coupled parsing to application state and prevented the main loop from inspecting the resulting command.

Make Parser a stateless command factory and let Athena execute each returned command. Represent invalid input as an InvalidCommand so parser errors follow the same execution path as valid commands.

Input currently detects bye itself, leaving one command outside the command
hierarchy and keeping loop control split across two classes.

Add ExitCommand and let Parser create it for a standalone bye. Athena
now executes the command and uses isExit to control its loop, while Input
only reads and frames user text.

Deadline currently keeps due dates as arbitrary text, so invalid
calendar values are accepted and dates cannot support date-aware
behavior.

Parse ISO yyyy-MM-dd input into LocalDate, persist its canonical form,
and render deadlines as MMM dd yyyy. Update UI and storage cases to
cover valid round trips and invalid dates at command and load boundaries.

Typed deadline dates are currently used only for validation and display,
so users cannot act on their calendar meaning.

Add an on yyyy-MM-dd command that selects matching deadlines in list
order and reports empty or invalid queries without changing stored tasks.
Cover the query path with UI, persistence, and packaged-build checks.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add event date and time handling
commitResults.messageBody:
Events previously stored their time ranges as free-form text. This meant
date queries could not include events and task times were not parsed
consistently.

Introduce a shared date-time value, accept slash or ISO dates with
optional 24-hour times, store canonical values, validate event ranges,
and include spanning events in date queries.

The new find command has the following features:
* Search task descriptions across all task types
* Case-insensitive substring match
* Reports no-match result
